 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Census of India 2011 revealed the approximate distribution of population among different Indian states as follows:
 
• **Andhra Pradesh**: Approximately 7% of the total population of India.
 
• **Maharashtra**: Approximately 9% of the total population of India.
 
• **Uttar Pradesh**: Approximately 16% of the total population of India, making it the most populous state in the country.
 
• This distribution highlights the significant demographic diversity and population density across Indian states as recorded in the Census 2011.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Census of India 2011**

 
 
• Conducted by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs.
 
• It is the 15th Census of India and the 7th post-independence Census.
 
• The total population of India as per the 2011 Census was approximately 1.21 billion.
 
 
 
• **Uttar Pradesh Population Highlights**
 
 
• With 16% of India's population, Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India.
 
• It has a population density of 828 people per square kilometer.
 
 
 
• **Maharashtra Population Highlights**
 
 
• Maharashtra, with 9% of India's population, is one of the leading contributors to India's economy.
 
• Mumbai, its capital, is the most populous city in India.
 
 
 
• **Andhra Pradesh Population Highlights**
 
 
• Andhra Pradesh, with 7% of India's population in 2011, was later bifurcated into Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in June 2014.
 
• The Census 2011 data reflects the population before this bifurcation.
